text:
maria: Quick question — do we have an agreed escape-hatch pattern for hosted->private fallback when we can't use a sidecar?

alex: Not a formal one. We've been relying on sidecars for creds + routing. Why the ask?

maria: Tracking a customer that can't run sidecars in their environment. They need a way to route to their private runtime with minimal infra changes.

sam: Could we add a header-based signal that the control plane understands and routes? E.g. X-RW-Mode: fallback-private.

li: Header feels simple but raises auth/cert issues. If we accept a header we need strict signing to avoid spoofing.

devon: +1 to signing. Maybe short-lived JWT issued by hosted control plane to the client, which the private runtime can validate via our PKI.

ops-bot: FYI: previous attempt with JWTs caused clock skew issues. Keep TTL >= 2m to be safe.

toshi: Also need to consider KV cache isolation: private runtime may not have same cache keys -> perf regressions.

alex: For routing, proposal A: header + signed token (no sidecar). Proposal B: ephemeral tunnel via control-plane proxy. Tradeoffs: A is lowest ops but weaker isolation; B is stronger but adds proxy ops.

maria: Can we sketch Proposal A? Minimal flow: client gets short JWT from hosted, injects header, request goes to control plane, control plane routes to private endpoint that validates token.

li: Validation will need to check token audience + sig + not-before/expiry. Also validate scope: read-only vs write.

devon: How do we rotate keys? We should integrate with existing KMS rotation. Private runtimes fetch current certs via our S3 bucket+signed URL or via SSM.

sam: One more: we need observability flags so we can attribute cost. Header should include route hint but we must strip before forwarding to customer backend.

maria: Example header idea:
```
X-RW-Fallback: jwt=ey...,route=private-eu,trace=xyz
```

toshi: Implementation note: don't log full jwt. Mask it in traces.

alex: Rollout plan: A/B alpha -> only opt-in customers. Add feature flag in Console and a per-tenant denylist.

li: Security review req'd. Also add circuit-breaker: if private runtime rejects >5% requests for 1m, auto-failover back to hosted or return 503 depending on tenant policy.

maria: Agreed. I'll draft an RFC with flow diagram, token format, validation rules, key rotation, and rollout plan. Any other blockers?

devon: Consider rate-limits: private runtimes might not accept same QPS. Need per-route quotas in control plane.

sam: Nice — also document downgrade semantics for KV cache misses: if private returns cache-miss we should avoid re-requesting hosted. Keep client-facing latency SLO.

maria: Thanks — will ping when RFC draft is ready. :slightly_smiling_face:
